input.question: Helicopter tail rotors? Why are they so important?
input.ground_truth: The torque required for the main rotor has an opposite torque acting on the rest of the frame. That is, if the main rotor is spinning clockwise, the rest of the frame is being torqued counterclockwise. The tail rotor acts to counteract the torque and keep the frame pointing in the right direction.

Okay! Imagine a helicopter is like a big flying bird.

The tail rotor is a small spinning fan at the back of the helicopter.

Here’s why it’s super important:

When the big blades on top spin to lift the helicopter up, they want to make the whole helicopter spin around too—just like when you spin in a circle with your arms out!

The tail rotor is like a little helper. It spins the other way to stop the helicopter from spinning around and around. That way, the helicopter can fly straight, just like you walking in a straight line.

So, the tail rotor helps the helicopter go where you want it to go, instead of spinning like a top!
